exposure: mode of delivery (Cesarean section, normal vaginal delivery)
outcome: non-aerated areas in gravity-dependent lung regions
cohort: A case-control study comparing 32 term neonates delivered by Cesarean section with 20 term neonates delivered by normal vaginal delivery.
finding: The mode of delivery significantly affects early postnatal lung aeration in term neonates, with Cesarean section neonates showing poorer aeration compared to those born vaginally.
mod_finding: Cesarean section neonates had greater non-aerated areas in gravity-dependent lung regions and lower changes in lung stretch compared to normal vaginal delivery neonates.
